newsitem.title: UK: Further oil price gains seen in 1996 - PIRA's Ross.
newsitem.headline: Further oil price gains seen in 1996 - PIRA's Ross.

text.p: The current high oil price may rise even more before the end of 1996 because of low oil stocks, but the outlook for 1997 is not so bullish, a leading U.S. oil analyst said on Monday.

Gary Ross, chief executive officer at Petroleum Industry Research Associates (PIRA), said the prolonged rally which took oil prices to post-Gulf War highs earlier this month, could have an adverse affect on oil demand.

"Inventories are extremely low and this is setting the tone of the winter market...we are going to see relatively high prices," Ross said. "There is no room for error. The market is very vulnerable to surprises because there is no cushion."
Global oil demand growth has been a robust three percent this year but there should be a slowdown in 1997, Ross told the International Herald Tribune Oil and Money Conference
Ross said demand for light oil products should fall 200,000-250,000 barrels per day (bpd) in 1997 while fuel oil demand could also slip assuming a normal winter.
Moreover, production from non-OPEC suppliers is expected to surge 1.8 million bpd from the current 46.7 million, pushing global supply to 72 million, Ross said.
"There is not a lot left over for OPEC if there is growth in non-OPEC supplies."
As such, he sees demand for OPEC oil including stocks to average 25.7 million bpd in 1997, below current output of 26.0 million.
"The core OPEC countries have decided to bleed oil into a hungry market, particularly to the Far East." --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7629
